question: What compatibility surfaces must the C++ compiler and Rust VM preserve together through the cdbc 0.2 variable-lowering upgrade?
decision: Adopt cdbc 0.2 as the emitted artifact contract with numeric local/upvalue/global slots while keeping strict cdbc-cache 0.2 schema 4, the fixed non-serialized native-name registry, and optional debug metadata. The reader keeps cdbc 0.1 name-based variable inputs as a construction-time compatibility path.

compatibility_cells.consumer: Rust parser, VM diagnostics, trace, debug, and profile
compatibility_cells.contract: debug_sources, debug_locations, and debug_ranges are optional; ranges are source-local half-open byte intervals
linked cdbc 0.2 is accepted after structural and reference validation; link rejects it as a non-module product
metadata-free cdbc 0.2 remains valid; debug sections are not required for dump, link, or run; legacy cdbc 0.1 inputs remain readable

compatibility_cells.consumer: Rust dump and linker; run rejects an unlinked module
compatibility_cells.contract: artifact: module products remain cdbc 0.2, validate module identity/dependencies before linking, and never execute as standalone programs

compatibility_cells.consumer: in-process host callers and command-line workflows
compatibility_cells.contract: the library facade is version 0.2 and the CLI preserves file IO, stdout/stderr, exit codes, dump/run/link/trace/debug/profile commands

compatibility_cells.consumer: compiler module-product emission and repair; Rust consumes products, not cache manifests
compatibility_cells.contract: cdbc-cache 0.2 schema 4 records source/public-interface/dependency/optimization identity, relative product paths, and product content digests; strict by default with --module-cache-fallback as the explicit repair opt-out

compatibility_cells.producer: C++ native lowering and Rust NativeSpec registry
compatibility_cells.consumer: Rust artifact verifier and VM dispatch
compatibility_cells.contract: native_call names use the fixed registered set; arity, callback, resource, and signature metadata remain VM-internal and are not serialized by cdbc 0.1

rules: X1r2 adopts cdbc 0.2 emission with numeric local/upvalue/global slots; the VM keeps a construction-time cdbc 0.1 name-based compatibility path for legacy inputs.
The compiler owns module-cache invalidation and source fallback; the VM validates and executes products but does not read .cdi or cache manifests to synthesize function bodies.
Debug metadata is additive and optional; metadata-free artifacts remain supported.
Native registry metadata is an internal VM contract until a future artifact version explicitly serializes a successor ABI.
A binary format, persistent session, GC, JIT publication, or host I/O capability requires a separate decision record.

required_existing_evidence: Rust library version and instance-isolation tests
fixed native registry and unknown-native rejection

out_of_scope: versioned native IDs or plugin loading
GC, cycle collection, relocating handles, or persistent VM sessions
changing module-cache fallback or strictness policy
